[6/7/22, 7:34:20 PM] Zalmen Ives: Sounds too fluffy

I think the point is that we should love our wife and children because that is the right thing according to the Torah.

The Torah is the source of all our morals and values and an unbreakable, unconditional love from spouse to spouse and from parent to child is a fundamental moral and value of the Torah, more than the value of loving all Jews.

But if that love tells us to violate the Torah or disobey G-d's commandments, we know that our love for our family is a human emotion just like our love for chocolate ice cream but a little stronger.

So the Tanya says we shouldn't love our children independent of our love of Hashem, but as part of it.

הנהלת "בית אהל חב"ד ליובאוויטש" שע"י האהל הקדוש של הרבי, מודיעה לציבור הרחב על פתיחת ההרשמה לאש"ל מלא בשבת קודש, יום ההילולא הכ"ח - ג' תמוז ה'תשפ"ב. 
כל אורח (אברכים בלבד, שלוחים, מקורבים וכיו"ב) צריך להירשם בפני עצמו. אלא אם כן זו קבוצה מאורגנת. התמימים נרשמים דרך מאגר רישום של ועד תלמידי התמימים העולמי. 
במקביל יופעלו 34 הבתים בסביבות האהל הק', ששייכים באופן פרטי לאנ"ש ושלוחים מרחבי תבל.

*Abortion*

https://www.estumult.com/topics/categories/abortion

The goal of Es Tumult Zich is to provide material from Torah sources, and from the Rebbe in particular, that relate to current events and issues. This way, we will have a framework within which to observe what is happening around us, anchored by the light and clarity of Torah. 

Of course, we do not venture to say that we know what the Rebbe’s position is on this topic or on any other event or subject. We are merely presenting various ideas that may have some bearing on what is occurring in the world today.

[6/15/22, 10:31:03 AM] ‪+1 (323) 877‑7703‬: Is quinoa haadama or shehakol?
[6/15/22, 10:41:27 AM] Shmully Litvin (KY): ‎This message was deleted.
[6/15/22, 10:42:09 AM] Shmully Litvin (KY): Haadama and Borei Nefashos, unless pureed and unrecognizable where it would be Shehakol.

While quinoa is technically classified by many as a grain, it is not one of the “five grains” (wheat, barley, spelt, oats and rye), nor is considered a semi-grain like Orez which is Mezonos. (There is a dispute whether this refers to rice or millet). Thus, it is Haadama.

https://asktherav.com/what-is-the-bracha-for-quinoa/

[6/15/22, 12:55:16 PM] ‪+55 11 93214‑3434‬: * Story of the Baal Shem tov traveling with his students. They stopped off in an inn and they were offered a meal with meat etc. Being the students of the Baal Shem tov and they had such high standards of kashrut they started questioning the shochet on all the laws and they were testing his level of piety and even after they sat down for the meal they were asking to see the knife and if it had any blemish etc. finally there was an old man sitting by the fire place who called out and said, “my fellow Jews, are you as careful with what leaves your mouth as you are with that which comes into your mouth? :)

* Story of the king who was so sick and needed milk from a lioness. Big reward. One man did a trick to get it and gave it food each day until slowly he got the milk. The night before he had a dream. Each limb was arguing that it's thanks to them. Then the tongue piped up and said its me. All other limbs were shocked. He said you wait and see. Next day he came to King and his mouth said here is milk from a dog. King got so mad and threw him in jail. All limbs agreed that he was the hero. Next day he corrected his mistake. Lesson is how careful we have to be with what we say and sometimes we may think that our speech doesn't make such a big difference but the truth is that it's so powerful.

שלח

שְׁלַח־לְךָ֣ אֲנָשִׁ֗ים וְיָתֻ֙רוּ֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ כְּנַ֔עַן אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֥י נֹתֵ֖ן לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִ֣ישׁ אֶחָד֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶחָ֜ד לְמַטֵּ֤ה אֲבֹתָיו֙ תִּשְׁלָ֔חוּ כֹּ֖ל נָשִׂ֥יא בָהֶֽם…
לְמַטֵּ֣ה אָשֵׁ֔ר סְת֖וּר בֶּן־מִיכָאֵֽל׃
(שלח יג, ב. יג.)

ביאור מאחז״ל (ב״ב ע״ג סע״ב) ואמר רבה בר בר חנה: זימנא חדא הוה קא אזלינן במדברא [פעם אחת היינו הולכים במדבר], ואיתלוי בהדן ההוא טייעא [ונתלווה עמנו ערבי אחד]….אמר לי אותו ערבי: תא אחוי [בוא ואראה] לך את מתי מדבר, [בני ישראל יוצאי מצרים, שמתו בשעתם במדבר]. אזלי, חזיתינהו [הלכתי, ראיתי אותם] ודמו *כמאן דמיבסמי* [ונראים היו כמו שמשתכרים].

שאלות;

א) מהו ביאור לשון חז״ל *כמאן דמיבסמי*?

ב) מהו הי׳ טעות המרגלים?

מרמז, שורש תיבת *דמבסמי* - *בסם* ראשי תיבות השם *סתור *בן *מיכאל

אגרות קודש ע׳ שנח
[6/18/22, 10:16:00 PM] ‪+1 (330) 861‑8770‬: *From the Rebbe’s Father זצ״ל*
שלח

Send agents to scout the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelite people.
From the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael.
(Shlach 13:2,13)

Explains the Gemara (Baba Basra 73b) And Rabba bar bar Ḥana said: Once we were traveling in the desert ….
That Arab said to me: Come, I will show you the dead of the wilderness, i.e., the Jewish people who left Egypt and died in the wilderness. I went and saw them; and they had the appearance of one who is *intoxicated*.

Question’s;

A) What is the meaning , they had the appearance of *Intoxicated*?

B) How could that generation err, they saw the great revelation on mount Sinai & Miracles?

A beautiful Remez; 
The Acronym of 
*סתור בן מיכאל* is *בס״ם* = *Intoxication*.

[6/19/22, 11:08:36 AM] ‪+1 (424) 244‑9872‬: This is what Hershy Drukman (France) wrote about his trip to the Ohel in Hebrew:
[6/19/22, 11:08:40 AM] ‪+1 (424) 244‑9872‬: שלום חברים,
עוקבי הסטטוס שביניכם שמו לב לתמונות שפירסמתי מנסיעה קבוצתית לרבי שערכנו בסוף השבוע שעבר. 

לשאלות כמה וכמה מידידיי השלוחים -  
ובפרט שהזמן גרמא, השנה שהיתה התעוררות רבה לנסיעה לרגל שנת ה120, ובשנה הבאה שנת הקהל - 
הנה סיכום קצר של הנסיעה. 

הגעה - יום חמישי בצהריים, עד ראשון בצהריים (במבט לאחור, שלושה ימים הם הנצרך בדיוק. לא פחות, ובעיקר לא יותר).

לינה, בבית נחמד ששכרנו ליד האוהל.

תכנית: 
קודם הטיסה הדפסתי חוברות על משמעות הטיסה לרבי. נתתי להם את החוברות בעליה למטוס. גם התוועדנו על כך במטוס.

אחרי התארגנות קלה בחדרים, לקחתי אותם לבית שליד האוהל. התפללנו מנחה והסברתי להם על המקום וקדושתו. עדיין לא ניכנס לאוהל עד למחרת בבוקר.

נסענו ל770. סיור כללי והסברים ב770 וקצת קינגסטון. סיימנו בארוחת ערב במסעדה בשכונה. מונית חזרה לבית שעל יד האוהל. הסברים והכנה לתכנית למחרת (מקוה, לא אוכלים וכו).
ליל מנוחה.


יום שישי:
מקוה.
שיעור חסידות בשבע וחצי.
תפילה שמונה וחצי.
אחריה, שוב הסברים והכנה על כתיבת הפ"נ ואופן הכניסה (גארטל למי ששייך, לא מדברים, בלי תמונות וכו). לקח את הזמן שלקח והאנשים נכנסו ברצינות הראויה. 

שעה אחר כך: נסיעה לשכונה.

קינגסטון. ביקור וקניה בחנות כובעים... סיור מפורט ב302 (בהזמנה מראש. עשה רושם עצום עליהם). קניות לשבת בסופרמרקט כשר חשוב (בדוקא. נהנו מאוד מהאווירה). 

ביקור בחדר שידורים (חשוב ומומלץ. בהזמנה מראש).

מנחה בבית הרבי (בהזמנה מראש). הכנו אותם מקודם על קדושת המקום, ועל סיפורים מבית הרבי. היה מיוחד. 

שלוש שעות לפני שבת נסיעה לאוהל. מנוחה, מקוה, טועמיה.

שבת באוהל:
מומלץ ביותר.

תפילות: 
בליל שבת התפללנו בד"א.
בשבת ביום התפללנו בטענט הראשון. תפילה כמנהג בית חב"ד ודאגתי שכולם יקבלו עליות (מי שלא הספיק בשחרית עלה במנחה). התרגשו מאוד. 

סעודת שבת באריכות. פארבריינגען. סיאסטה.

המלצה: לא לסמוך רק על האוכל במקום (שהוא מצוין ותודה רבה על זה), אלא גם לקנות תוספות כמו, משקה, יינות, עוגות וכו לטועמיה, ארוחת בוקר, ועוד כל מיני נשנושים לפארבריינגען. להשאיר חלק בדירה וחלק לשמור במקרר ליד הטנט.

שיעור לפני מנחה, אחרי מנחה פרקי אבות. מעריב הבדלה.

מוצאי שבת: חלקם נסעו לפיצה קרובה, חלקם הלכו לישון מיד.

ראשון בבוקר:
שחרית, שוב כניסה לאוהל.
נסיעה ל770.
כניסה לחדר הרבי. (בהזמנה מראש, עם הכנה נכונה כמובן).

קינגסטון, מתנות.
ארוחת צהריים,  ביקשתי מכל אחד לומר דברי סיכום, וכולם היו בהתעוררות עצומה. 
נסיעה לשדה.

המלצה חשובה באם אפשר: להביא קבוצה הומוגנית ככל האפשר. קבוצת גיל, תחומי התעניינות דומים וכו, כך קל יותר להתאים להם את התכנית. 

*כמובן כמובן שאני רק מספר על התכנית שלנו* אין כאן שום תורה מסיני וכל אחד יכול לכול לנסות להתאים את הנסיעה באופן שיתאים לקבוצה שלו. 

למעוניינים במספרי טלפון ופרטים נוספים להזמנות והרשמה לכל המקומות שהוזכרו לעיל, אנא שלחו בפרטי ואשלח לכם בשמחה.

עד כאן.
בהצלחה רבה לכולם.

[6/19/22, 11:34:51 AM] ‪+1 (204) 869‑7631‬: Dear Shluchim

It is in our darkest hours when coming together as a family is most important

Shluchim are indeed a family. 

We share in each other’s simchas, and regrettably, often time are forced to share in each other’s sorrow and hardships. 

Just a few days ago, our very own Rabbi Chanoch Piekarski lost his dear wife Shevy, as she returned her pure soul to its Creator following a devastating illness, leaving him and their 7 beautiful children. 

We turn to you, our fellow Shluchim, with a chance to be there for one of our own in his time of need. 

A campaign has been set up at https://raisethon.com/shevy/shluchim-achdus to help ease the financial burden on Shevy’s family in these difficult times, as well as ensure continued financial stability for the foreseeable future.

We ask you to please consider contributing and to also setup a team page, as a representative from your city of Shlichus, and communicating the importance of this fundraiser to your friends, family, and community. 

Indeed, we are all one family. 

We hope you will consider creating a team page by visiting the above link and clicking “create team”

May we only share in each other’s happy occasions from henceforth. 


Sincerely,

Rabbi Shmuel Kaplan Maryland
Rabbi Leibel Baumgarten East Hampton, NY
Rabbi Yossi Liberow Barranquilla, Columbia
Rabbi Yosef Yitzchok Greenberg Alaska
Rabbi Berel Goldman Gainesville, Florida

[6/21/22, 11:08:35 PM] Mendel Brandwine: *האם תרצה להיות שותף לסחיטה?*
_כך תוכלו להיות שותף פעיל למעשי סחיטה למשפחות אומללות, לאיומים על מוסדות חינוך, ולעוד מעשים נהדרים כאלו_

במשך חודשיים האחרונים, חסידי חב"ד מכל העולם הזדעזעו כששתי משפחות חב"דיות ברוכות ילדים איבדו הורה, שתיהם צעירים ר"ל.

לאחרי שתי הטרגדיות, נפתחו קמפיינים לטובת המשפחות, לעזור להם בשעות הכי קשות שלהם.

מסוף העולם עד סופו, אנשים נרתמו לעזור, לסייע וליתן יד.

אך, היו אלו שראו בכל הסיפור רק עוד הזדמנות להרוויח לעצמם, על חשבון המשפחות האומללות.

בשתי המקרים, הבעלים של האתר Collive הזהירו את מארגני הקמפיינים שאם הם ישלחו כלום לאתרים האחרים, הם לא יעזור להקמפיינים, ואדרבה...

בשתי המקרים, המשפחות הצריכו ללכת "מאחורי הגב" של RaiseThon, מארגן הקמפיינים - שהשלים עם הדרישות - ולשלוח כתבות לאתרים אחרים.

נכון, באמצע שבעה ר"ל על יקיריהם, זה היה צריך להיות על הראש שלהם.

וכל זה בנוסף לאינספור סיפורים על איומים (כן, איומים) למוסדות חינוך, לשלוחים ולחסידים שהעיזו לשלוח לאתרים אחרים.

***

נגיד את זה באופן ברור:

מי שמשתף פעולה עם האתר Collive פעולה, מי ששולח להם כתבות, הרי הוא *נותן להם את הכח* להמשיך במעשי עוולה אלו.

בכך אתם נותנים להם היכולת לאיים על המוסד הבא, לשחק עם הטרגדיה הבאה ה"י כדי להרוויח ממנו.

הרי אילו אנשים עם מצפון היו מפסיקים לשלוח להם, בתוך פרק זמן די קצר ישאר האתר בלי הכח למעשים אלו...

ולכן, נקודה למחשבה:

האם שווה כמה קליקים להיות שותף איתם?

[6/24/22, 2:40:03 PM] ‪+1 (917) 474‑3257‬: Google gave me this: 
https://www.oxfordchabad.org/templates/articlecco_cdo/aid/304578/jewish/The-Rebuilding-of-Jewish-Life-After-The-Holocaust.htm

An interesting episode occurred when the Rebbe was still living in Paris. The Nazis demanded that everyone register with the authorities and state their religion. When an official visited the Rebbe’s apartment building, requesting registration, the Rebbe was absent. As a favour, to spare the Rebbe of the danger of being registered as Jewish under Nazi occupation, his neighbour wrote ‘Orthodox (Church)’. Upon his return, when the Rebbe heard of this, he went to the registration office and corrected his identification to Jewish. Although this would have potentially saved his life, he would not compromise his Jewish identity even on paper.

[6/26/22, 9:21:31 AM] ‪+44 7961 914795‬: Godi and Shlomo

It was 1989.  An Israeli Defense Force soldier named Godi Remon was shot by an Arab terrorist outside of the town of Ramallah. The Arab gunman assumed he was dead and moved on.

Shortly afterward, a young Israeli named Shlomo Bergman happened to be driving by and saw Godi bleeding on the ground. He brought him into his car and sped off to the nearest Israeli hospital. He underwent surgery and survived. Shlomo left the hospital minutes before the parents of the victim arrived.

Godi's mother was bothered by not being able to thank the mystery person who saved her son and tried unsuccessfully for a year to find out who he is. But to no avail.

Godi's parents put up a sign at their grocery store which they owned in the city of Ashdod, describing what happened. They reasoned that Israel is a small country and eventually they might find the person who saved their son.

Months passed with no response. Finally, one morning about a year later, Anat Bergman, Shlomo's mother, was visiting friends in Ashdod. She entered a grocery store and noticed the sign hanging by the door of the store. She asked the store owner who put up the sign. When Godi's mother said it was her, the two mothers embraced for a long time.

Then Shlomo's mother said, “Look at me -- you don’t remember me?” “No", Godi's mother said, "I’m sorry. Did we meet before?"

"Yes," Shlomo's mother said. "Twenty years ago I used to live around here and I came all the time to buy basic groceries. One day you noticed that I looked really down and you asked me why I was down. I told you that I was going through a very difficult time and on top of that I was pregnant with my first child and planning on having an abortion because I could not with the mental and financial pressure. As soon as I said “abortion” you called your husband over and the two of you didn’t seem to care about your own store but sat and patiently listened to my story and my challenges. I still remember what you said."

“You told me that it is true that I was going through a hard time, and that you understood how stressed out I was, but sometimes the greatest things in life come through the biggest difficulties. You spoke of the joy of being a mother and that the most beautiful word to hear in the Hebrew language is “Ima” (mother) when spoken by one’s child... You explained how all the challenges pale in comparison with the inner joy coming from raising a child, from embracing your little one, from cultivating a living miracle. You explained how with each child born, a new channel opens up in our lives, generating a greater consciousness, and more livelihood. You both spoke for a while with so much empathy, love, and sensitivity, until I was convinced that I should have this baby."

Shlomo's mother continued, "I gave birth to the baby twenty years ago. My son Shlomo wouldn’t have been alive if not for you. Two decades later, he was the one who saved your son, Godi’s life.”

You see, you saved my son's life; now he saved your son's life.

[6/27/22, 11:25:21 PM] ‪+1 (323) 369‑6325‬: I think it's important not to conflate Hashkafa and Halacha. Two very distinct areas of Torah.

From a Hashkafic standpoint Torah is unequivocently pro life and against pro choice, understood in it's most literal sense. Yet, this does not reflect the Halachic view if obortion is allowed/mandated or not. The discussion if a fetus is considered a life/human/person etc. is purely a Halachic discussion and has nothing to do with the Torah's view of being prolife. 

Once you have the Torah's outlook on obortion, then the discussion starts when according to halacha an obortion is allowed or not, which is a case by case basis and no blanket statements can be made.

The Torah's outlook/Hashkafa is what you should and shouldn't do. The Halachic discussion is what you can and can't do.

[7/1/22, 3:48:11 PM] ‪+1 (347) 446‑0479‬: DO YOU REMEMBER THE REBBE?

This Shabbat is the Rebbe's 28th Yartzeit-Hilula.

Even if you never met the Rebbe, do you remember him?

When providence puts you on a flight next to a fellow Jew, do you remember the Rebbe and see how you can help them feel more Jewish?

When the dishwasher repairman says “Shalom,” on his way out, do you remember the Rebbe and offer him your Tefilin for a Mitzvah? 

When painful news comes (G-d forbid) do you remember the Rebbe and remind yourself to think good so it’ll be good?

When great news comes and you’re flying high, do you remember the Rebbe and create some good news for someone else? 

When Passover rolls around, do you remember the Rebbe and make sure all the Jews you know have Shmura Matzah and a place at a Seder?

When life is calm and quiet, do you remember the Rebbe and remind yourself that G-d has assigned a special purpose to every day? 

When you’re anxious about all your needs, do you remember the Rebbe and think about everything G-d needs from you? 

When you prepare to light the Shabbat candles on Friday, do you remember the Rebbe and put a few coins in Tzedakah first?

When you go about doing a Mitzvah - any Mitzvah - do you remember the Rebbe and do the Mitzvah energetically and with obvious pleasure?

When go to work, do you remember the Rebbe and keep and eye out for opportunities to share the light and warmth of Torah and Mitzvos to one more thirsty soul?

When you learn something, do you remember the Rebbe and teach it to someone?

When you think about what you really, truly want with all your heart, do you remember the Rebbe and think, "I really want Moshiach!"?

When you feel your heart overflowing with joy and pride and gratitude at all the blessings in your life, do you remember the Rebbe and direct your resources and energies toward helping others and bringing Moshiach?

Some of us remember the Rebbe's scholarly talks. Others recall the brisk and energetic gait. Some remember the exuberant singing at the Farbrengens. Others remember the complete focus at the Sunday dollar line. Some remember the proud, unbowed posture. Others remember the smile that lit up the world. 

Those memories warm the heart. Those memories of things about the Rebbe are priceless. But there's a difference between the Rebbe's qualities and the Rebbe.

The Alter Rebbe once played with his grandson, a little future Rebbe. "Where's Zaide?" asked the grandfather. The toddler pointed to the Alter Rebbe's beard, eyes etc. but each time the grandfather said no, that's Zaide's beard, those are Zaide's eyes etc. where is Zaide? The boy turned away, seemingly done with the game, and the Alter Rebbe turned away too. But then the boy said, "Zaide!" His grandfather turned to him and the boy triumphantly declared, "There is Zaide!" 

When we remember the good times, the holy days, the exciting moments, the uplifting experiences - we are remembering the Rebbe's light, the Rebbe's warmth, light and wisdom.

But when, at the right moment, we remember to live the life the Rebbe taught, there, as the little boy said, is the Rebbe, in all hs glory, alive and well in our good thoughts, words and deeds.

So let's remember to remember the Rebbe who never forgot anyone. The common expression regarding a Tzadik's memory is Zecher Tzaddik L'Bracha - the memory of a Tzaddik shall be a blessing. Let's remember the Rebbe and every time we do, make sure that memory becomes a tangible blessing in life: in our life, the life of our loved ones, and in the life of all the people around us.

Let's remember the Rebbe and bring Moshiach already.

Rabbi Eli Friedman
Chabad of Calabasas

[7/3/22, 10:42:44 AM] Shmully Litvin (KY): Any highlights from farbrengens you attended?

At our kiddush farbrengen, one of the guests shared his connection to Chabad. He began by saying that when he was young, he had many opportunities to visit the Rebbe. But he never went. In fact, he used to make fun of those people who went to stand in line to get a dollar...

20 years later, he is traveling the world, and stops on an island in the Philippines. Naturally, he is at the Chabad House. The shliach asked him for a favor. He had to go to Israel for 2 weeks, and asked him to keep an eye on his house, open the doors, etc.

Then covid hit. And the shliach couldn't return home. The shliach told him that the Chabad house was his house, and he could choose to be open or close, whatever he wanted.

After some thought, he decided that he will keep the doors of Chabad open. This raised a difficult decision. He wasn't frum. How could he lead the Chabad House? He decided that outside of his bedroom he would keep everything. 

He then went downstairs, and came face to face with the picture of the Rebbe. He said "I looked at the Rebbe, and his eyes were saying to me: Really? This is what you are going to do?" So he answered the Rebbe's image "you are right, I will do it the right way". 

And so for the next 9 months he was the Chabad House. He helped arranged burials, brisim, minyanim, etc.

When pesach came, he decided to hold a Seder, on of the only ones in the world that year. 25 people scheduled to come to the seder. But he had no matzo. 

He remembers thinking come on, I didn't do all of this not to have matzo on pesach! After calling friends, 2 days before pesach 4 soldiers of the Filipino army marched into the Chabad House with a huge box of matzo. What they thought was so important to hand deliver from the capital to this island was anyone's guess. 

He said there were many more miracles and moments that he would share at a later point, but finished with the message. Lchaim, there is a Rebbe, and he is available for all of us to connect to. 

May we be reunited with the Rebbe with the coming of Moshiach and the 3rd Beis Hamikdosh before you can like this comment.

2. Jewish Life grants are available for organizations who:

a.	Foster Jewish identity among young people, including the children of intermarriage and interfaith families, in the United States through outreach and engagement tailored to the interests and needs of the participants. 

b.	Connect individuals to the Jewish community and create a welcoming and open atmosphere within the community to nurture a sense of belonging to and a commitment to the Jewish people and Israel.  

c.	Professionalize the field of Jewish and Israel education.

d.	Foster a celebration and respect for Jewish diversity in Israel by encouraging Jews of all denominations to practice understanding and mutual respect

e.	Cultivate the legitimacy of and participation in diverse Jewish living and learning options in Israel, empower voices of Jewish pluralism, and seek to establish an environment in which these diverse Jewish options may thrive.

f.	Expose secular Israelis to the core texts and values of the Jewish tradition and encourage an exploration of their Jewish identity. 

https://slifkafoundation.org/jewish-life/

Solicit via LOI to programofficer@slifkafoundation.org

Each grant allows providers to apply for up to $1,000 per licensed childcare slot, at a maximum $100,000 per program.

https://www.cfmt.org/story/childcaretennessee-tdhs-offering-grants-to-create-expand-child-care-capacity/

*****

As in past years, this year Purim Project customers can benefit from direct home deliveries of ORT Atlanta’s Honey From The Heart exclusive honey jars on Rosh Hashana alongside a Purim Project (aka your Shana Tova project) campaign*. There are two attractive options for you to choose from:

1. Bulk order your honey: Order all your honey jars in bulk to a single address by September 1st, and run your Shana Tova project as usual. You will receive the honey jars about one month before Rosh Hashana and you'll distribute them to members alongside your greeting cards, as usual. (Bulk orders after August 1st are subject to availability.) 
2. Direct Delivery by Honey From The Heart: Share your Member List (export the list directly from Comsend) with Honey From The Heart by July 25th and run your Shana Tova project as you do normally. You distribute the greeting cards (by email or paper cards) and Honey From The Heart delivers the honey jars directly to your members in time for Rosh Hashana. 
https://campaign-image.com/zohocampaigns/485652000013735020_zc_v30_ort_honey_small.jpg
Pricing
Honey From The Heart jars cost $8.50, including delivery (whether in bulk or directly to your members).

Contact
You can contact Honey From The Heart directly at support@orthoney.com with any questions on their role in delivering honey jars and to register for their services. Be sure to tell them that you’re a Purim Project customer.

You're invited to respond to this email with general Rosh Hashana campaign questions. 


 * This offer is available only in the continental United States

All the best,

Jeff and your Purim Project team

[7/13/22, 1:46:13 AM] Meir Pape: In addition to the good pirushim brought above from actual meforshim,
 I always make sure to preface, that the mishna was written to men (meaning assuming mostly men would read it). If it would have been written to women, it would've said: don't chatter too much with men.

[7/19/22, 9:22:33 AM] Zalmen Ives: Btw, on the topic of this chat's new name, besides for the discussion about what to ask the rov, there is also benefit in knowing which rov to ask.

I was in the sukkah of Yitzchok Zirkind a"h for a Y"T meal. During the meal, 3 separate individuals came in to ask shaalos. One he sent to Raabi Schwei, one to Rabbi Gorelik and the 3rd to another. We asked מאי האי? He explained he sent them to the rov he knows to be meikel in that area.

I asked Rabbi Braun if it is OK to ask different rabbonim depending on the question, and he said it's fine. As long as you don't ask two rabbonim about one question.

I'm not saying to make a practice out of this, or not to have "your rov", but if it can be done for someone's שמחת יו"ט, then it can be done for an integral area of our shlichus.

[7/19/22, 9:28:49 AM] Chaim Markovits Chaim Hillel: Reminder. 
 *Super easy hack*
*But takes courage.*
*Do you have courage?* 

If you're thinking in advance 

And you're brave enough to make the calls and send the emails 

Someone here posted that the advertisement company Lamar with billboards all over USA has a policy for 501c3 that they may give you free or discounted space. 

Now's the time (well in advance of RH/YK/Sukkos) to reach out to your local office and form the relationship with the regional and local decision makers. 

And ask them to run an ad for you about your high holidays or presence in town or whatnot. (Think Hebrew school, camp, moshiach, purim, chanukah, pesach, yud shvat, hey teves, chof Ches Sivan - the opportunities are endless!)

Here's the process (that I did) step by step:

1. Google Lamar in town
2. Call the number (leave a message - rabbi x calling to speak to the manager - Google his name in advance, it's typically public information)
3. (I didn't meet face to face) get the person on the phone. Ask, "I saw online that your company offers ad space for non profits. What's the process to earn that?"
4. Follow the instructions given. They'll provide you a template (jpg with sizes and dimensions required) and you fit your ad in that. 
5. Send it back to them In a timely fashion.

Hacks
6. Ask what locations are available.
7. Ask if it'll be a digital or printed sign 
8. Be sure to include a website and telephone number in your ad.
9. Be sure to go in to visit the manager and other staff you've be working with. Show them appreciation. They just gave you $1,000 donation! 
 

10. If you've done this, or successfully do it bc of this post, *pls post your ad on the chat* (not the digital image - i wanna see the billboard!)

[7/19/22, 1:29:52 PM] ‪+27 65 944 5633‬: *Tanya*
I use these Seforim to prepare for Tanya class:
1. Tanya
2. Chassidus Mevueres
3. Mesaprim Tanya
And I use the bold of 4. Lessons in Tanya when teaching it if I’m not teaching orally

How I prepare:
For the *toichen* of the Perek
1. Read through the whole Perek in one shot and write a few line summary to crystalize that exercise. 

If I’m unsure / have time, I read  Chassidus Mevueres’s Kitzur of the Perek at the end. I also enjoy their intros when I get to it.

2. If there’s a particular section I don’t understand or want to learn more about I read the biur of that from CM

For the *inspiration* / take-home:
3. Read the italic sections of CM
4. Read (and type up) the stories of Mesaprim Tanya and any other stories I can think of that drive home the nekuda.

5. If I’m on the road alone and in the mood I listen to YYJ on Chassidus.org or our RY Lipskier to spice the upcoming classes with some more stories / jokes

Be kind to yourself, and remind yourself that you're doing your part. You're doing your best. The rest is out of your control, and ultimately in Hashems hands.

[7/20/22, 11:46:32 AM] ‪+1 (310) 666‑2302‬: Looking for a Bar Mitzvah curriculum?
[7/20/22, 11:50:23 AM] ‪+1 (240) 690‑1285‬: . I do it with my bar mitzvah kids.
[7/20/22, 11:53:07 AM] Meir Pape: 1. Try to get inside the building and knocking on doors. Don't ring doorbells from outside the building and hope people will let you in.
2. If there's a guard, wave with a big smile and walk right past.
3. Take a picture of the names directory at the front of the building, if there is one.
4. Write down everything!! Perhaps even record and write down afterwards.
5. Have a clear message. Not just "we're looking for Jews". (I'd be comfortable saying something more like "we're coming to share Jewish summer greetings with our local neighbors", but really any classic merkos shlichus pitch works). After that have a plan, what's if it's going well where are you taking it, tefillin, giving books, Mezuzah, etc.
6. Don't expect people to let you inside their house. It doesn't mean they don't like you, they may have another person there, they may be embarrassed of their messy quarters, or for any other reason. 
7. One trick I found to have people let you in, (only use if it's already going well, and it just happens to be they don't realize they could invite you in), ask if they have a restroom you can use.
[7/20/22, 11:53:15 AM] Meir Pape: Use at your own risk!

[7/22/22, 6:20:36 PM] ‪+1 (718) 313‑8814‬: Similar point
As one of the Alter Rebbe’s wealthy chassidim advanced in years, he was able to marry off his children and establish them in business. A generous man by nature, when the responsibilities of his immediate family became less pressing, he committed himself to pay for the weddings and dowries of his relatives’ children.

Suddenly, however, his business affairs took a sharp turn for the worse, and instead of being affluent, he found himself in debt and unable to meet his commitments. Before his financial situation became public knowledge, he hurried to Liozna to receive advice and blessings from the Alter Rebbe.

At yechidus, he poured out his heart to the Rebbe, saying that he was prepared to remain impoverished himself, but he needed to pay his debts and honor the commitments that he had made to his relatives.

The Alter Rebbe responded: “You are speaking about what you need. But you have not given a thought to what you are needed for.”

The chassid fainted; the Alter Rebbe’s attendant had to help him out of the Rebbe’s room. When he came to, he began to devote himself to prayer and study, without thinking of his business concerns.

After the chassid had conducted himself in this fashion for some time, the Alter Rebbe sent for him. Standing before the Rebbe, the vision of his previous yechidus flashed in his mind, and he could barely muster the strength to look the Rebbe in the face. This time, however, the Alter Rebbe spoke to him gently: “Now you appreciate G‑d’s truth.... You can return home...; may G‑d grant you success.”

The man made his way home and discovered that the gloomy picture he had seen previously could be corrected. A few favorable strokes of fortune had given him the opportunity to right his financial course.

[7/25/22, 10:28:52 AM] ‪+1 (412) 580‑7981‬: *No Mitigating Mitzvah*

_A letter from the Lubavitcher Rebbe about one who attends services on Shabbat morning and then goes to work_

 . . . With respect to your question . . . about a person’s dilemma, who prays in the synagogue on Shabbat and then opens his store:

You did not specify the purpose of your question. It would seem that this is in the purview of the archangel Michael who records the merits of the Jewish people. 

Now, the Mitzvah that he fulfilled is a Mitzvah and he will certainly receive his reward for it. It is self understood, however, that this does not help him, nor does it diminish the harshness of his transgression when he desecrates the Shabbat. Especially if he sits in his story, which is in the public eye.

It is the duty of his acquaintances to explain that he can’t exempt himself. The fact that he prays in the synagogue doesn’t diminish the harshness of his subsequent desecration of Shabbos. Elaboration on this point is surely superfluous.

Source, Igros Kodesh 7 #1904

[7/25/22, 2:41:46 PM] Meir Pape: I once spoke to a person who had this exact experience as you described (got very involved, then realized there's no way he's continuing to live with his non Jewish wife and advance his yiddishkeit so he stopped the yiddishkeit).

There are 2 points to consider:
1) it's not all or nothing. Even if 99% of your life is a non Jewish one, and 1% you embrace your neshama, when you engage in that 1% your connection to hashem is 100%.
2) it's normal that someone doesn't want to be a hypocrite. But that's only where you can pick and choose to live one lifestyle or another. Here though, regardless of how uncomfortable it makes his feel, hiz yiddishkeit is just not something it's possible to shove under the rug. His neshama isn't going away, it's his identity, it will always be there, and it will resurface one day or another. This is so part of him that he can't just "remove" himself from it. So ignoring it is a (perhaps short term) cover-up which isn't being real to himself. Better live a hypocritical life, and at least nurture your neshama somewhat, than to totally oppress it.

When I spoke to this person, he found both points very enlightening, and admitted he never saw it that way. (He still didn't come back though...)

[7/26/22, 9:51:59 PM] Meir Pape: I would (preferably get on the phone with him and) explain that:
1. You're so so so excited about his new baby, and can't wait to embrace him as family!
2. The bris is a very deep sensitive Jewish practice with has religious requirements, such as it has to be done on the 8th day, not before. Read it together inside in god's words to Abraham at the end of parshas lech lecha :)
3. Many brisim have no one present, all that are needed are the parents, the baby and the Mohel. Few friends and a breakfast is all that's needed to make it as meaningful and special as can be!
4. Some people make a follow-up bris party few months down the line, to invite family and friends. (I've seen the Rebbe writing to suggest this, not regarding bris but re bar mitzvah and upsherin).
5. Judaism strongly discourages doing it in the hospital, because if done in the hospital it has to be done again after the 8th day (with a slightly different procedure).
6. If medical concerns - think about it: if you have a specific need, do you go to a generic doctor, or someone who specializes in this specific need? Doctors in the hospital, mainly do other things, they occasionally do this also; a Mohel - does countless of these procedures, it's his expertise.

[7/29/22, 1:25:59 AM] ‪+1 (408) 766‑2343‬: FW: 
Question of the Week: Our baby boy was born yesterday and we are deliberating whether to do a traditional Bris with a mohel, or have it done by a surgeon in hospital. Now the question I have is, would you accept me and my son into your community if he is not snipped by a mohel?

Answer: Mazel tov on becoming a father! I hope your wife is doing well and wish you both only happiness and much nachas!

Let me say outright, you and your son will always be welcome, no matter what you choose. I don't put any barriers up for someone to be a part of our community. 

As a parent, you need to make many decisions that will impact your child's future. This is one of them. Here are the things you need to know before deciding what to do: 

- A surgical circumcision is not a Bris. Apart from the missing blessings and prayers, the actual cut may be different. Which means one day when your son realizes that he didn't have a Bris, he may require a rather unpleasant procedure to get it fixed. At the very least he will need some blood to be drawn and a blessing said. No big deal when you are a baby, but not quite as easy when you're older.

- A Mohel is not an amateur. Quite the opposite. The average surgeon might do a few of these every now and then. An experienced mohel does them almost daily, and has performed hundreds, or possibly thousands, over the years. 

- Many Mohels are also medically qualified. Some are themselves surgeons, who will perform a Bris in their rooms if you prefer. 

- The risks involved with either procedure are minimal, but surgical circumcision could arguably be riskier than a traditional Bris, as more complications can arise from giving a baby an anaesthetic than from just a clean cut alone.

- The Bris is a tradition that stretches back almost four thousand years. It connects us and our child with all past generations of Jews, who gave their children a Bris under all circumstances. Your son will enter the covenant that started with the first Jew, Abraham, and continues to this very day. The spiritual power of a Bris cannot be matched by a surgery that is essentially cosmetic. 

Think it through carefully. You don't want your son turning to you years from now and asking, "Why didn't you give me a Bris with a Mohel? Now I have to go and get it done properly!" On the other hand, if you do it the right way now, he will never turn to you and say, "Why didn't you circumcise me in hospital? Now I have to go and get a local anasthetic to make up for it!"

Give your son a Bris, and you give him four thousand years of Jewish identity that will stay with him forever. Don't leave it for him to fix later. This is one of those things you only want to do once. 

Good Shabbos,
Rabbi Moss

[7/31/22, 10:54:36 AM] ‪+1 (929) 245‑2241‬: *The Pitch:*

_Acts of Random Kindness become Act of Routine Kindness. The result: a kinder human being._

Beyond academic achievement, schools are always looking for opportunities to inculcate a sense of moral and societal obligation within their students. The goal being to raise the next generation of upstanding citizens and leaders. ARK is the latest worldwide trend in that space. 

By giving children an ARK charity box and encouraging them to take it home, have it proudly displayed, and to deposit a coin every day, we are teaching them:

•	That action speaks louder than words. When we do good deeds, we become good people.
•	That each individual, and indeed every action, is valuable. It doesn’t matter what you have or how much you give. It only matters that you give.
•	That there are others in the world who also have needs, just like we do.
•	That in a world of digital interactions, money, being in need, and giving, are as physically real as the ARK box and the charity they deposit.  
•	Everyone can and should be a contributor to society. 
•	Giving isn’t limited to when there is someone in front of us asking. It’s a moral privilege and duty upon us to seek out those in need and give before we’ve been asked.

All of this is achieved through consistent action that, with Gd’s help, becomes second nature. This kind of actionable teaching method that goes home, is far more powerful than anything taught using traditional methods in the classroom. 

Even if charity is never deposited in the ARK, the tangible and visible object stands as a reminder to the children and their families about their place in society, and those in it that are needy. 

This helps the student switch from “receiving consciousness” to “giving consciousness”.

[8/1/22, 10:11:14 PM] Meir Pape: There are many budget printers out there. And most of them you can get toners from knock-off brands that do the same job as the more expensive company brand.
Specs I found most helpful:
How many ppm (speed of papers printed per minute) - check both single sided and double sided.
How many papers can fit nicely into the output tray before you they start getting caught in one another.
Same with input tray how many papers.
Can it print envelopes, cardstock.

I agree that for color you'd want a separate inkjet printer

וכיון שהתורה מבהירה אפילו "מכה אשר לא כתוב בספר התורה הזאת" – היו צריכים למצוא בתורה נתינת מקום לקבוע ענינים גם על הגזירות כו' שהיו בדור האחרון.

יא. קושיא זו – בנוסח אחר – מצינו במאמר של אדמו"ר הזקן בתורה אור:
מבואר שם הידוע שכללות עבודת האדם בעולם היא לברר את ניצוצות הקדושה שנפלו למטה, שהם במספר רפ"ח ניצוצין, "וכשיוגמרו הבירורים יבוא משיח". ואיתא בספרים שבמשך מאתיים ועשר שנים של גלות מצרים נתברר מספר גדול של ניצוצים – ר"ב ניצוצים, כמרומז במ"ש "וגם ערב רב עלה אתם", ונשאר לברר רק פ"ו ניצוצים.
וא"כ נשאלת השאלה: כיון שבמשך מאתיים ועשר שנים של גלות מצרים, הספיקו בני ישראל לברר ר"ב ניצוצים, בהיותם במספר ששים ריבוא – הרי לפי חשבון זה, בודאי שבמשך זמן הגלות שנתארך כו"כ מאות שנים, ובני ישראל הם במספר גדול מששים ריבוא כמה פעמים ככה, היו צריכים מזמן לסיים את בירור הניצוצות, ובמילא היתה צריכה להיות כבר הגאולה האמיתית והשלימה. ומהי הסיבה שלא מצליחים להשלים ולסיים את בירור פ"ו הניצוצים הנשארים?!
ומבאר על זה אדמו"ר הזקן, שכשם שבכל ענין ישנו כלל שכולל בעצמו כו"כ פרטים, כן הוא גם בענין הניצוצות, שהמספר רפ"ח הוא מספר הניצוצות הכלליים, שבירידתן למטה "נתחלקו ונתפרדו עוד ביותר לאלפים ורבבות",
ובהתאם לכך יש גם חילוק בעבודה דבירור הניצוצות ע"י בני ישראל – שנשמות גדולות וכלליות, יכולה כל נשמה לברר ניצוץ כללי (קודם שנחלק לריבוי פרטים), משא"כ כאשר נתמעטו הדורות ונתמעטו הנשמות, אזי בירור ניצוץ כללי הוא שלא לפי כחה ואפילו שלא לפי ערכה של נשמה אחת פרטית, שבכחה וביכלתה לברר רק פרט אחד מריבוי הפרטים שנתחלקו ונתפרדו מניצוץ אחד כללי.
ולכן: בזמן גלות מצרים שאז היו בני ישראל במספר ששים ריבוא – הנה ששים ריבוא נשמות אלו היו נשמות כלליות (כמבואר בתניא ש"ששים ריבוא נשמות פרטיות אלו הן שרשים, וכל שרש מתחלק לששים ריבוא ניצוצות וכו'"), ולפי גדלם הי' בכחם לברר ר"ב ניצוצות כלליות; ולאחרי כן, כאשר נתמעטו הדורות ונתמעטו הנשמות, אזי נתחלקו ונתפרדו פ"ו הניצוצות הנשארים לאלפים ורבבות וריבוא רבבות ניצוצות, כדי שיהי' בכחם של הנשמות הפרטיות (ופרט דפרט כו') לברר אותם.
יב. ומזה מובן גם חומר הענין שנעשה מצד חסרונו של יהודי אחד מהדורות הראשונים – להיותו נשמה כללית.
וכמו שהענין הוא גם בגשמיות – שכתוצאה מהחסרון של יהודי אחד בדור שביהמ"ק הי' קיים, נעשה חסרון גדול ביותר בדורנו זה:

[8/4/22, 4:41:16 PM] ‪+1 (305) 365‑6744‬: This ended up being a long post. Here's the TL;DR version: It's how to get $40,000 of credit card processing for 1.2375%. Plus a bunch of other perks for free.

I've been meaning to share this with fellow shluchim for a while. I've used this for the last few months and it saved us money. 

There is a membership called Founders Card. It is not a credit card. It doesn't affect your credit score, and it isn't a way to borrow money. The term "Card" is actually a bit misleading (although they do send you a card). It is a membership service designed to benefit entrepreneurs and business owners.

The idea behind Founders Card is that you pay to join this membership service and they negotiate all sorts of discounts and benefits with various companies.

The membership offers hundreds of different benefits, some more valuable than others. There are a lot of travel benefits, such as status at various car rental companies (free status at Hertz, Sixt, Avis) and hotel chains (free status at Hilton, Omni), discounts on certain airlines, and discounts and privileges at many hotels.

It also offers various business benefits, like discounts at:
- Office Depot 
- UPS 
- Dell
- Fiverr (including years free membership)

There are many other benefits that may have potential value which I haven't really looked at yet.

However, the real money-saving value this membership offers - and this is the point of my post - is $40,000 of fee free credit card processing. You can get $20,000 free credit card processing with Stripe (new and existing accounts) and an additional $20,000 free credit card processing with Square (new accounts only), for a total of $40,000 of fee-free credit card processing. 

I have already used this benefit and it absolutely works. I can charge someone's card $100 and receive the full amount in my bank, no fees at all.

The membership costs $495 a year if you are referred by an existing member (you can use my link below). Without a referral it costs $690 for the first year and then $595 per year. 

If you use the full $40,000 of fee free processing, the $495 membership fee ends up being the equivalent of paying 1.2375% for credit card processing, which is about half of the normal rates! Plus you get all the additional perks for free.

Please note that as of now the free credit card processing is a one-time benefit, meaning the membership may only be worth it for you for the first year. They are constantly adding new benefits though, so there may be some new benefits that will make it worth continuing. Either way, you can always cancel at any time.

The referral sign up link is https://founderscard.com/membership?code=FCAVREMEL132

There is a referral benefit I hope to receive by my link being used, so please use the above link. It will also give you the discounted membership price. 

There is a higher tier of membership called Founders Card Elite, which costs $995/year. This can potentially be worth it for you (for the first year), as they offer an additional $30K of fee free processing with stripe (for a total of $50K), in addition to the 20K with Square. An extra $500 fee for $30K of processing works out to 1.66% for the next $30K. So if you typically process close to $70K in a year this would be worth it for you.

However, even if it is worth it for you to pay the $995 for Elite membership, I would not recommend upgrading to FC Elite off the bat. If you sign up for regular membership they will often send you a promotional discount to upgrade to Elite for even less. And if they don't, you can always upgrade later for the $500. 

Feel free to pm me if you have any questions.

I hope this helps many of you save money. Much hatzlocha in your shlichus!

[8/11/22, 6:59:45 PM] Shmully Litvin (KY): Powerful Side Point 👍👍

[The mitzvot of honoring parents is one of the only ones in the Torah that is guaranteed the most sought-after reward of all: longevity. I heard an on-point explanation of the link between respecting parents and longevity: respecting parents takes time, a lot of time. Dad calls at exactly the most stressful time and asks to meet you, deliver a package to someone, or get medicine from the pharmacy while dealing with Medicaid. You tend to apologize that you don't have the time and maybe turn to another sibling.
That is why G-d promises to give you long longevity, to return all of time you dedicated to your parents. He will extend your shelf life in this world and thus you will find enough time to make up for the so-called lost hours...].

וכיון שמצוה פ׳ הנה בעבר לא קיים אותה (מאיזו סיבה שתהי') – למה יקיימה בעתיד? (2)

וכנראה גם אותה מבלבל בזה (בכדי למנוע ממנה וממשפחתה שי' ברכות השם בגו"ר) והמענה *המוכיח* שכ"ז  *שקר גמור* .

(1) באם לא הי' *ח"ו* דתי – לא הי' מקיים כל מצוה כלל.

(2) רצון ותשוקת *כאו"א מבנ"א* צו וואַקסן לא רק בגוף אלא גם בנשמה בהבנה, במדות טובות, בצדקה, וכיו"ב, ועי"ז מוסיף השם בברכותיו.

[8/18/22, 10:37:26 PM] ‪+1 (224) 212‑0576‬: Dear Friends,
With great pleasure, we present this beautiful Jewish Art Calendar for the year 2022/2023 – 5783, our gift to you for the New Year. We hope 
that the beauty and wisdom surrounding these pages will inspire you to delve deeper into our rich Jewish heritage.
This year, 5783, is a year of “Hakhel”—gathering and unity.
In biblical times, once every seven years—during the Hakhel year—all Jewish men, women, and children would gather together in the Holy 
Temple to hear the Torah being read by the kingof Israel.
This unique experience underscored the principle that we are all one. Whether they were Sephardic or Ashkenazic, secular or religious, liberal 
or conservative—this gathering was for everyone.
In the absence of our Holy Temple in Jerusalem, we can’t observe Hakhel in the literal sense. But it remains a year when as a nation, we join as 
one to reaffirm our common heritage and destiny. The Lubavitcher Rebbe taught that during this year we join in mini-Hakhels with friends, 
neighbors, family, or any Jew we meet. This Hakhel year, let us gather our “whole mishpacha”;irrespective of our differences, we are all one.
As we enter our 4th year of Chabad in Arlington Heights, we recommit to this fundamental principle of being here for everyone in the 
community, building a home where every Jew feels proud to belong.
We extend our thanks to the advertisers and sponsors in this calendar and to all of our supporters. With your continued assistance, we hope to 
strengthen, broaden and deepen the scope of our work. As we approach Rosh Hashanah, we wish you and your loved ones a happy, healthy 
and sweet new year. May you be inscribed in the book of life, blessing, prosperity and peace.
Warmly,

[8/19/22, 2:59:32 PM] Shmully Litvin (KY): Here's a great paragraph from an article on chabad.org

Once a year, on Yom Kippur, we are forced to face our inner demons. We are forced to confront out shortcomings and stand up to them. We are given the opportunity to feel real regret and remorse and make positive resolutions for the coming year. This yearly introspection, subconsciously at least, ensures that we live a life of accountability. We know that once a year we will have to account for our actions, not only to G‑d, but to ourselves as well. So, Yom Kippur helps to make sure that we do not get carried away with life to the extent that we are unaware of our shortcomings; it ensures that we maintain not only our spiritual health but our personal decency as well.

- food that I want to eat (chicken or steak for dinner)
- beds that I want to sleep in or a hotel that my wife would be comfortable in.
- a car that I wanna drive (suv rental - no trashy donations)
- my personal credit card "please buy whatever you want" (no group has abused this yet).

We take them to the local restaurant as a goodbye
And give both $100-150 at any bookstore they choose.

[8/25/22, 6:06:12 PM] Menachem Aron: Yes. They won't be perfect.
But they will get things done that you will never get done. I've been using a VA for about 8 months now.
They manage all my data entry, and keep track of every meaningful interaction that takes place.
That's what best works for me. They can do repetitive or 'boring' tasks efficiently, and it's also a huge relief to have someone that you can past in jobs too. For example, preparing a weekly email. Or creating a form in your website for rosh hashana.
They will need some basic training.
Every chabad atarts with 1 or 2 ppl running it, but it doesnt take much to get things out of control with too much to do. Older shluchim were more into doung every kast thing themeslevs, but thats not a very productive way of running a moisad. You will need to hire, and all the chisronos you are listing will apply to pretty much anyone that you hire. So yes there is a learning curve, but ultimately a big benfiit as you can offload mundane tasks and focus on the important stuff.

[8/30/22, 6:50:54 PM] ‪+1 (718) 308‑5516‬: Sharing if this helps anyone:

I haven't yet moved down to my makom Hashlichus, but I got a call about a woman, a Holocaust survivor in hospital.

Besides doing everything I could for her and her family, which included sending another Shliach on an eight-hour return trip to visit her, I got a local woman involved. She went to visit, said some prayers etc.

And I had this woman call other people in the community to wrote cards, give flowers (one person sent over matzo ball soup..) and through that, together with me using it as an excuse to contact people, I found more Yidden I never knew about and got existing people more involved, showed them how Chabad cares about people (when her family called the local temple they told her they can't help as she isn't a dues paying member 😳).

So besides for hopefully cremated, it became a great way to engage the community even being 2,500 miles away.

[9/5/22, 6:13:47 PM] ‪+1 (929) 245‑2241‬: Has been discussed in the past in this and/or other groups.

Some takeaways:

1) It seems like accuracy depends on the area, if you are in or near a center of Jewish life it will likely be more accurate.
2) in your town itself it might be more accurate in the nicer areas of your town.
3) negotiate the price with them over the phone. You'll get a much better deal.
4) IMHO even with the inaccuracies it gives you something to start working with.
5) you can also ask them to get email addresses for an additional fee, though they won't have as many as the regular list.

7) every new year get the new movers list

An older rabbi and his wife had hired a young woman orphan to help in their house. One day the wife noticed that a piece of her jewelry was missing, and she was convinced that it was the young woman who had stolen it. So she brought it to the attention of a beis din. [9/8/22, 11:59:38 PM] Menachem Aron: «Postal Greeting»,

The High Holidays are almost upon us.

In just a few days, Rosh Hashanah will begin, and we’ll collectively turn the page on our calendars to a new year.

The past year, and in fact 18 months, have been a challenging time for all of us. Rosh Hashanah is a time for us to reset, to start over anew. Every night, we go to sleep, every seven days we begin another week, and every twelve months we begin another year.

These cycles that have been built into our lives are the greatest kindness. They constantly give us a chance to restart, to begin anew, and give things another chance. When we begin a new year, we are given another opportunity to renew our relationships, renew our commitments, and renew our connection to our Judaism.

Rosh Hashanah is not just the first day of the year, but indeed it is the “Head” – “Rosh” in Hebrew – of the year. Much like the head controls the body and its functions, Rosh Hashana is the day that sets the tone for the coming year.

Beginning with Rosh Hashana, followed by Yom Kippur, and finally Sukkot, the coming month is packed with special days and unique practices. The enclosed “High Holiday Handbook” and included treats will assist you in kick-starting the new year, and will provide great insight into the meaning, observances, and customs of the upcoming Holiday season.

We take this opportunity to wish you and your loved ones and very happy and sweet new year – a “Shana Tova U’metuka”. May the new year bring much blessing and happiness to your lives and may all your prayers throughout the Holiday season be answered with prosperity and goodness.

Sincerely,

Rabbi Menachem & Shevi Aron and family
[9/8/22, 11:59:45 PM] Menachem Aron: September 2022 - Elul 5782


«Postal Greeting»,

 The Jewish near year is right around the corner!

Sounding the Shofar (ram’s horn) is one of the special things we do on the Rosh Hashana. It’s a simple sound, said to recall the cry of the soul as it prepares for the day of Judgement.

An interesting fact about the Shofar is that one needs to use a horn that has a bend in it. It cannot be completely straight like a trumpet, but must curve upwards towards the end. Many times, our lives have twists and turns. Not always is everything so straightforward. The necessity of having a bend in the Shofar teaches us that we must have these “twists” in our lives. They bring out the best in us, and let our true colours shine.

Rosh Hashanah is not just the first day of the year, but indeed it is the “Head” – “Rosh” in Hebrew – of the year. Much like the head controls the body and its functions, Rosh Hashana is the day that sets the tone for the coming year.

Beginning with Rosh Hashana, followed by Yom Kippur, and finally Sukkot, the coming month is packed with special days and unique practices. The enclosed “High Holiday Handbook” and included treats will assist you in kick-starting the new year, and will provide great insight into the meaning, observances, and customs of the upcoming Holiday season.

We take this opportunity to wish you and your loved ones and very happy and sweet new year – a “Shana Tova U’metuka”. May the new year bring much blessing and happiness to your lives and may all your prayers throughout the Holiday season be answered with prosperity and goodness.

Sincerely,

Rabbi Menachem & Shevi Aron and family
